header.running_head: Honouring the Weak and Poor Muslims

blocks.text: fact is that whichever one of you sins out of ignorance[^1] and then repents and (makes) amends (for his sin), (he should remember that) Allaah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful (Allaah will therefore forgive him)."

Hadhrat Khabbaab (RA) related further, he says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ then threw the paper away and called for us. When we came to him, he said,' - Peace be upon you'. We then drew so close to him that our knees touched his. It was the practice of Rasulullaah ﷺ when he sat with us to stand up and go when he needed to leave. However, Allaah then revealed the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِيْنَ يَدْعُوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدٰوةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيْدُوْنَ وَجْهَهٗ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنٰكَ عَنْهُمْ
blocks.text: '(O Rasulullaah ﷺ) Restrain yourself with (in the company of) those who, seeking His pleasure, call to (worship) their Rabb morning and evening and do not shift your attention from them.'

Thereafter, whenever we sat with Rasulullaah ﷺ and it reached the hour when he would usually get up to leave, we would stand up and leave him. Had we not done this, he would restrain himself as long as we did not stand."[^2]

Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) narrates that there came to Rasulullaah ﷺ some people (new Muslims) whose hearts Rasulullaah ﷺ was still winning over to Islaam. Amongst them was the likes of Uyaynah bin Hisn and Aqra bin Haabis. They said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Why don't you sit at the front of the Masjid and keep away from us these people and the odour of their cloaks." They were referring to the likes of Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA), Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and other poor Muslims who wore woollen cloaks because they could afford no better (they could not afford finer material and therefore perspired with the thick wool). "If you do this," they continued, "we could sit with you, discuss with you and learn from you." It was then that Allaah revealed the verses:

blocks.arabic_text: وَاتْلُ مَآ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ كِتَابِ رَبِّكَ لَا مُبَدِّلَ لِكَلِمٰتِهٖ وَلَنْ تَجِدَ مِنْ دُوْنِهٖ مُلْتَحَدًا وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِيْنَ يَدْعُوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدٰوةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيْدُوْنَ وَجْهَهٗ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنٰكَ عَنْهُمْ تُرِيْدُ زِيْنَةَ الْحَيٰوةِ الدُّنْيَا وَلَا تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهٗ عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوٰىهُ وَكَانَ أَمْرُهٗ فُرُطًا
blocks.text: (O Rasulullaah ﷺ) 'Recite (to people) what (revelation) has been revealed to you from the Book of your Rabb (the Qur'aan). There is none who can alter His words (Allaah's words in the Qur'aan and His promises) and you will certainly not find another place of refuge
All sins are committed out of ignorance because no person will sin if he really knows the punishment for the sin.

Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.146). Ibn Maajah has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.6 Pg.56). Ibn Abi Shaybah has also reported a similar narration, as quoted in Kanzul Ummaal (Vol.1 Pg.245).
